questions.stem: What happens to the non-nitrogen part of an amino acid after deamination?

options.text: It is converted to ammonia and then to urea
It can be used for respiration or converted to fat
It is stored as protein in the liver
It is excreted by the kidneys as urea

questions.explanation: After the amino group is removed during deamination, the remaining carbohydrate portion of the amino acid can be used in respiration to release energy, or it may be converted to fat for storage.
